bounds.domain: One hosted McpService, one HTTP server, one discoverable tool, one temporary transport, one initialization and one stop. An unrelated action can replace the lazy action in its registry slot once. Discovery can succeed or fail. Stop closes publication before removing both connected and lazy tool registrations. A pending initialization can settle after stop.
bounds.implementation: Five loopback tests use the real SDK and StreamableHTTP transport. They stop after lazy registration, during a held resource reply, and after actual temporary transport close with the lazy-registration continuation held. A local runtime registry fixture checks that teardown preserves an action with the same name and a different identity. One supplemental case stops a public lazy connection after the service has started.
limitations: Several SDK discovery requests are one bounded outcome. The transport flag represents the locally tracked transport. Physical closure if the SDK throws, duplicated close calls and stuck external operations are outside this model.

Schema caching, active tool calls, repeated runtime starts, independent reconnects and per-entity connections are outside this projection. Existing retry tests supplement the transport cases without proving the retry ladder.
This is the hosted runtime MCP client. Configured upstream proxy sessions, the retired SSE route, provider effects and credential ownership are separate.

assumptions: No fairness. One independent same-name replacement can occur after lazy publication. Other runtime mutations of that slot are outside the bound.
Weak fairness of the tracked transport close outcome and stop acknowledgement. A transport close responds. The pending discovery continuation need not settle before stop.
Weak fairness of the discovery outcome, temporary close request and reply, lazy publication and cancellation continuation. Discovery can fail, and stop can cancel it.
No fairness. The transport close or stop acknowledgement can remain pending.
